item.title: Bolsonaro's departure from Brazil puts spotlight on US' Latin America strategy, Brazil's pursuit of strategic autonomy: experts
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-28 18:05:00
Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva (center) delivers a speech after winning the election in Sao Paulo, Brazil, on October 25, 2026. Photo: VCG Brazilian opposition presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro has left Brazil for the US following his defeat to incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, with the Trump administration confirming that it would grant visas to him and his family, Reuters reported on Tuesday, in a dramatic development that has brought renewed attention to Washington's relationship with Brazil's right-wing political forces and the future of US influence in Latin America. Chinese and Brazilian experts reached by the Global Times said the developments reflect broader tensions between Washington's efforts to maintain its regional influence and Latin American countries' growing determination to pursue independent foreign policy. They noted that Lula's renewed mandate could provide fresh momentum for Brazil's pursuit of strategic autonomy, including through stronger regional coordination and more diversified partnerships with countries across the Global South, while maintaining relations with traditional partners. According to Reuters on Tuesday, Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, left Brazil after failing to comply with a Supreme Court order requiring him to surrender his passports in connection with a money-laundering investigation. Bolsonaro has denied wrongdoing. Lula, speaking in Brasilia, said he had just heard that Bolsonaro had left the country, and called it shameful, saying he should have stayed in Brazil and proved his innocence. The development followed Trump's remarks on Monday that the Brazilian vote "looked like another rigged election," although he presented no evidence to substantiate the allegation. Bolsonaro initially refused to concede defeat and called for the results to be annulled, but his Liberal Party subsequently acknowledged Lula's victory. Asked at a regular press conference on Tuesday about Trump's claim, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said, "We respect the independent choice of the Brazilian people." A clear setback Evandro Menezes de Carvalho, an invited professor at Macao Polytechnic University and professor of international law at Fluminense Federal University in Brazil, told the Global Times that Flávio Bolsonaro's defeat also represents a political setback for the US, which had sought to weaken Lula's government through tariffs, sanctions and visa restrictions. Carvalho argued that such measures had failed to produce significant political effects in Brazil, suggesting that external pressure has limited effectiveness in shaping the domestic political choices of Latin America's largest economy. Pan Deng, director of the Latin America and Caribbean Region Law Center at the China University of Political Science and Law, told the Global Times that the Trump administration had viewed the prospect of a right-wing government in Brazil as an opportunity to strengthen regional strategic alignment on trade, supply chains and broader geopolitical issues. Lula's victory has complicated those calculations, particularly given Brazil's position as Latin America's largest economy and a major political actor in the region, he said. Pan noted that Washington has increasingly relied on tariffs, unilateral sanctions and political pressure to advance its regional agenda. Such policies may secure short-term concessions but risk generating longer-term resistance among countries concerned about their economic interests and independent decision-making. Ronnie Lins, director of the China-Brazil Center for Research and Business, offered a similar assessment while emphasizing the enduring importance of Brazil-US relations. "The consolidation of Lula's presidency represents a clear setback for Trump administration's regional strategy, particularly because it rules out the prospect of an ideologically compliant government in Brasília," Lins told the Global Times. Nevertheless, he stressed that presidential rhetoric and long-term national interests should not be confused, as Brazil and the US maintain extensive economic, diplomatic and institutional connections. Countries across the region now have a broader range of economic and commercial options, including expanding partnerships with emerging economies, which have strengthened their bargaining position in international affairs, he said. Lins warned that excessive reliance on tariffs, sanctions and political pressure could encourage Latin American countries to diversify their international partnerships more rapidly, strengthen their engagement with BRICS and place greater emphasis on national sovereignty. He also argued that Washington's long-term influence would increasingly depend on its ability to offer meaningful economic opportunities while respecting the political independence of regional partners. Strategic autonomy Lula has repeatedly emphasized that Brazil should not become the "backyard" of any foreign power, a position that has gained renewed attention amid the election controversy. Pan said this election highlighted the importance of sovereignty and economic independence in Brazilian political debate, as voters weighed domestic development priorities alongside concerns about external political pressure. He argued that Brazil's pursuit of strategic autonomy should not be interpreted as an attempt to distance itself from any particular major power. Rather, it reflects a pragmatic effort to preserve independent decision-making and maintain diversified international partnerships. Lins likewise cautioned against interpreting Lula's reelection solely as a rejection of US influence, noting that economic stability, social policies and governance also played important roles in shaping voters' choices. Diversified partnerships Beyond the immediate political controversy, analysts said Lula's reelection could reinforce Brazil's efforts to pursue a more diversified international economic and diplomatic agenda, with cooperation among Global South countries playing an increasingly important role. Lins said Brazil's broader significance lies in demonstrating that national sovereignty and active participation in the global economy are not competing objectives, but can reinforce each other. Rather than defining its international position through rivalry between major powers, Brazil should use its diplomatic flexibility to advance practical development priorities, including infrastructure, industrial modernization, technological innovation and greater participation in global value chains, he noted. While Lula's reelection provides continuity in Brazil's current diplomatic direction, his administration will continue to face political constraints from a Congress in which conservative and center-right forces retain considerable influence. Nevertheless, Pan argued that differences in political ideology do not necessarily translate into opposition to international economic cooperation, particularly when such partnerships support employment, export earnings and industrial development. China represents an important example of these broader economic interests. According to Brazilian government figures released in January, China remained Brazil's largest trading partner for the 17th consecutive year in 2025, with bilateral trade reaching $171 billion, up 8.2 percent year-on-year. Brazilian exports to China totaled approximately $100 billion, accounting for 28.7 percent of the country's total exports, compared with around $38 billion exported to the US, according to the figures.

item.title: Real Madrid apologizes to Chinese people over Mbappé's inappropriate remarks amid mounting criticism
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-28 17:51:00
Kylian Mbappé of Real Madrid reacts during the La Liga match between FC Barcelona and Real Madrid at Camp Nou Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Barcelona, Spain. Photo: VCG Real Madrid on Wednesday apologized to the Chinese people over inappropriate remarks by forward Kylian Mbappé that have sparked widespread outrage in China, with the club expressing respect for the country's history, culture and citizens in a statement published on its official website. "Real Madrid C.F. wishes to express its apologies to the Chinese people for the discomfort that may have been caused by the recent words of our player Kylian Mbappé," the club said in the statement released on Wednesday. "Our club maintains a profound respect for China, its history, its culture and its citizens, as well as for the millions of Chinese fans who feel affection for and admiration for Real Madrid," it added. The club said it joined the public apology previously issued by Mbappé, noting that the player had expressed regret for his words and reiterated his respect for the Chinese people. Real Madrid also reaffirmed its commitment to "the values of respect, coexistence and understanding between cultures," expressing its wish to continue strengthening the bonds of friendship and affection connecting the club with China and its citizens. The statement came after Mbappé issued a public apology on Tuesday over inappropriate comments in a video interview that circulated online and triggered a backlash among Chinese fans. The French player acknowledged that his remarks had been "ill-judged" and had hurt people in China and Chinese communities around the world. The controversy has had commercial and broadcasting repercussions. Three Chinese companies - Dongpeng Beverage Group, dairy producer Mengniu and cheese maker Milkground - announced that they were ending their partnerships with the football star. China's state broadcaster China Media Group also announced the suspension of broadcasts of La Liga matches amid the controversy. The China Football Association said on Tuesday that it had made serious representations to Real Madrid and demanded formal public apologies from both the player and the club. On Wednesday, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said China attaches importance to the apology made by the person concerned when asked to comment on Mbappé's apology for his erroneous remarks.

item.title: German president's first day of visit in Anhui highlights Germany's 'dual-track' approach to China: expert
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-28 17:36:00
German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier visits the Volkswagen Group China Technology Company (VCTC) and tries a vehicle associated with CARIZON, a company specializing in advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS), on October 27, 2026. Photo: Steinmeier's Instagram account "Essentially, China's first opening-up to the West took place here," German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier wrote in an Instagram post on Tuesday after completing the first day of his visit in Hefei, capital of East China's Anhui Province. His itinerary included a visit to the former residence of Li Hongzhang, a tour of an urban water management system and a stop at a major Volkswagen research and development center, reflecting a willingness to gain a deeper understanding of China in the complex context of China-Germany relations, a Chinese expert said. In a post titled "History, Urban Development and E-Mobility," accompanied by 19 Instagram Stories documenting the first day of his visit, Steinmeier said he began his China trip in Hefei, visiting the former residence of late Qing Dynasty statesman Li, who met Otto von Bismarck in Germany in 1896, and Luogang Central Park, a former airport site featuring a water management system to prevent flooding and improve the urban climate. He ended the day at Volkswagen Group China Technology Company (VCTC), the automaker's largest R&D center outside Germany, which focuses on electric mobility. "Relations between Germany and China are so diverse that they do not fit into a simple black-and-white pattern," Steinmeier said. He noted that his visit would therefore extend beyond economic hotspots and deliberately take a broader view of China. Anhui was a fitting choice, he said, "because, essentially, China's first opening-up to the West took place here." The choice of Hefei as the first stop of the visit is noteworthy, as it offers a perspective on China that goes beyond high-level meetings and symbolic diplomatic engagements, Feng Zhongping, director of the Institute of European Studies at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, told the Global Times. The itinerary reflects an effort to gain a deeper understanding of China through its history, culture and economic development, sending a positive signal that Germany is willing to better understand the country amid the complexities of current China-Germany relations, Feng said. The expert noted that Germany is increasingly seeking to maintain economic ties with China while protecting its own industries, reflecting a dual-track approach to bilateral relations. Photos accompanying the post also showed Steinmeier himself trying out a vehicle associated with CARIZON, a company that specializes in advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) and autonomous driving technologies. The automotive industry is a pillar of Germany's economy, and the rapid development of electric vehicles has made cooperation with China increasingly important for German companies. While European countries remain concerned about competition and the protection of domestic industries, they also recognize that China is an indispensable partner in tackling shared challenges, Feng added. Ahead of the visit, Steinmeier said on social media on Monday that the trip would focus on Germany's multifaceted relationship with China and the challenges facing the two countries. In an earlier Instagram post outlining his visit to Anhui, Steinmeier said that in Beijing, the second stop of his visit, the program includes talks with Chinese leaders and a speech at Peking University on China's role in the world. On Friday, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said at a regular press conference that the sound and steady growth of the comprehensive strategic partnership between China and Germany, the world's second- and third-largest economies, not only serves the interests of both countries, but is also what Europe and the world hope to see. "We hope to work with the German side to take this visit as an opportunity to cement mutual trust, deepen cooperation and seek joint innovation, so as to make greater progress in bilateral relations, contribute to steady and sustained growth of China-Europe relations, and bring fresh energy to the world," Mao added. German media outlet DW described the state visit as taking place "in uncertain times," noting that Germany is seeking alternative partners in the region while also seeking to maintain good ties with Beijing. The Süddeutsche Zeitung (SZ) similarly noted that bilateral relations are "diverse but also complex," while trade ties are being recalibrated. The Europe-China Forum 2026, scheduled for November 5, will address these questions. According to the organizers, the issue is not only how Europe and China can manage their differences, but also how they can build a relationship capable of navigating global transitions together over the next 50 years. Steinmeier's visit comes as European countries continue to consider how to manage relations with China amid economic interdependence and strategic differences. The challenge is not simply whether to cooperate with China, but how to sustain engagement while addressing trade disputes and concerns over market competition, Feng said.

item.title: China urges Germany, EU to be objective, rational after Merz's claim of 'unhealthy' dependence
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-28 16:29:00
Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun China urges Germany and the EU to remain objective and rational, work with China in the same direction and resolve differences through dialogue and consultation, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on Wednesday, in response to reported remarks by German Chancellor Friedrich Merz calling for reduced dependence on China. During a visit to Singapore on Tuesday, Merz warned against full economic decoupling from China, but claimed that Europe and Asia must reduce "unhealthy, one-sided dependencies" in supply chains, technologies and raw materials. He also asserted that Germany's policy toward China was "coming of age" and was aligned with the EU, according to Reuters. Asked to comment on the remarks at a regular press briefing, Guo said that China has consistently advocated openness and cooperation and is committed to working with all parties to maintain the stability and security of global industrial and supply chains, while providing greater momentum and certainty for the world economy. The Chinese and German economies, as well as the Chinese and EU economies, are complementary and their industries are deeply interconnected, with practical cooperation between them rooted in mutual benefit and win-win outcomes, Guo noted. "China hopes Germany and the EU will remain objective and rational, work with China in the same direction, become reliable and predictable partners for each other, resolve differences and disagreements through dialogue and consultation, jointly maintain the stability and smooth functioning of global industrial and supply chains, and provide greater certainty for business cooperation," the spokesperson said. item.title: Chinese rescue team detects signs of life beneath collapsed building in Kenya's Nairobi
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-28 13:53:00
A Chinese rescuer (2nd R) communicates with a local rescuer at the site of a building collapse in Eastleigh, Nairobi, Kenya, on Oct. 27, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Jianfei) A Chinese disaster rescue team has detected signs of life beneath the rubble of a collapsed building in Kenya's capital, Nairobi, raising hopes of locating survivors as joint rescue operations continue, officials said Tuesday. Anthony Muchiri, emergency operations manager of the Kenya Red Cross and the official in charge of the organization's operations at the site, told Xinhua that members of Blue Sky Rescue, a Chinese humanitarian disaster relief organization, have detected two distinct life signals deep beneath concrete slabs and twisted metal. "By using the specialized equipment from China, rescuers have narrowed their search to specific locations, replacing the previous approach of clearing broad areas of debris," Muchiri said. Blue Sky Rescue rescuers arrived at the site on Monday with specialized life-detection equipment, including high-precision radar life detectors, seismic acoustic sensors, and snake cameras. Zhang Yuran of Blue Sky Rescue said that the team had been conducting life-search work and cooperating with several rescue teams on site. He added that rescuers had begun clearing access routes to reach the two locations where signs of life had been detected. Machinery provided by Chinese companies has also supported the rescue operation. William Sifuna Watitwa, a staff officer for the Nairobi North sub-region, said that China's Xuzhou Construction Machinery Group had provided an excavator and a 25-tonne crane to support the search efforts. "The excavator played an instrumental role in rescuing two people trapped beneath the debris on Saturday," Watitwa said. The Kenya Red Cross said on Tuesday evening that 20 people remained missing. The multi-story building collapsed on Friday in Eastleigh, a high-density commercial and residential suburb in Nairobi. Machineries provided by Chinese companies are seen at the site of a building collapse in Eastleigh, Nairobi, Kenya, on Oct. 27, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Jianfei) A machinery provided by China's Xuzhou Construction Machinery Group (XCMG) is seen at the site of a building collapse in Eastleigh, Nairobi, Kenya, on Oct. 27, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Jianfei) A Chinese rescuer (in blue) works with other rescuers at the site of a building collapse in Eastleigh, Nairobi, Kenya, on Oct. 27, 2026. (Blue Sky Rescue/Handout via Xinhua)

item.title: Safeguarding national sovereignty a shared duty of all Chinese people including Taiwan compatriots: mainland spokesperson on Kevin Tsai's remarks
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-28 12:04:00
Photo: Chen Binhua, spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office Asked about a recent social media post in which Kevin Tsai Kang-yong said he had "never supported Taiwan independence," Chen Binhua, a spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, said on Wednesday that safeguarding national sovereignty and territorial integrity is a shared obligation of all Chinese people, including compatriots in the Taiwan region. The spokesperson said that China has always respected and protected the legitimate freedom of speech and expression of Taiwan compatriots. However, there is no room for ambiguity on fundamental issues involving national sovereignty, security, and development interests. Chen also expressed the hope that members of Taiwan's entertainment industry would take pride in being Chinese, do more to deepen the bonds of kinship between compatriots on both sides of the Taiwan Straits, and promote cross-Straits exchanges and cooperation. China has always welcomed Taiwan compatriots to visit the mainland for sightseeing, to see family and friends, and to participate in exchange activities. China will continue to support greater exchanges and cooperation between entertainment industry professionals on both sides of the Taiwan Straits, so they can share the cultural markets on both sides and jointly promote and pass on Chinese culture. Previously, Tsai's appearance at a campaign event for a diehard "Taiwan independence" separatist sparked widespread criticism. Tsai attended the campaign headquarters launch of Shen Pao-yang, a Democratic Progressive Party candidate for Taipei mayor, who has been designated a diehard "Taiwan independence" separatist by mainland authorities. Several brands operating in the Chinese mainland have cut ties with Tsai recently following the incident. For example, Chinese clothing brand Inner Mongolia Erdos Garment Co said in a statement on October 14 that it remains firmly committed to the one-China principle and Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory. Noting that Tsai had only served as a host at a previous one-off event, had no long-term partnership and cannot represent any stance of the company, ERDOS said that the company and its brand took immediate action to remove all relevant materials, and it also reserves the right to pursue legal action. His actions have also prompted widespread criticism from netizens. Some netizens have urged brands to step up scrutiny of the political motives of relevant entertainers. On October 14, Chen, the spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office responded to Tsai's appearance at the campaign event for a diehard "Taiwan independence" separatist, saying that safeguarding national reunification and opposing "Taiwan independence" represent the shared will of all Chinese people, and no individual or force can benefit from the mainland's development while colluding with "Taiwan independence" separatist forces and being two-faced.

item.title: Desert brine from former 'sea of death' feeds fields across China
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-28 08:36:00
This photo taken on Sept. 5, 2026 shows a factory of the SDIC Xinjiang Luobupo Potash Co., Ltd. in northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region. (Xinhua/Zhang Xiaocheng) Four hours south of Hami, after a long drive across the barren Gobi Desert of northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, a sweep of blue-green water appears on the horizon. It is not a lake. These are evaporation ponds, stretching across more than 160 square kilometers at a sprawling potash operation in Lop Nur, once known as the "sea of death" for its extreme aridity and forbidding terrain. The desert is also home to Lop Nur Town. There are no families who have lived there for generations -- nearly everyone went there in the new century because of the potash resources beneath Lop Nur's salt crust. POTASH BENEATH DESERT Potassium is a key plant nutrient, helping crops develop stronger stalks and fuller grain. For years, China had relied heavily on overseas potash, with domestic self-sufficiency long below 30 percent. Exploration in the 20th century uncovered a world-class sulfate-type potassium-rich brine deposit in northern Lop Nur. But finding the resource was one thing, and producing fertilizer from it on an industrial scale was another. There was no established industrial process elsewhere to copy. The location also posed its own problems. Two decades ago, there were no roads, little fresh water and no settled population. "When I first came to Lop Nur, the wind blew sand straight into the face. You could go through all four seasons without seeing any green," said Liu Qinyong, who has worked at SDIC Xinjiang Luobupo Potash Co. Ltd. for more than 20 years. "Everything had to be brought in from outside." SDIC is short for the State Development and Investment Corporation. The first batch of Lop Nur-brand potassium sulfate was produced in 2003. The company later built a production complex with an annual capacity of 1.2 million tonnes, which reached designed capacity by the end of 2011. The company has so far produced over 27 million tonnes of potassium sulfate, with its products accounting for nearly half of China's potassium sulfate market. TURNING HARDSHIP INTO ADVANTAGE Production in Lop Nur relies heavily on both evaporation and time. Brine pumped from underground moves through a four-stage evaporation system, where different salts crystallize as the concentration increases. It takes nearly two years before potassium-bearing minerals are ready for processing. These minerals then undergo further processing, including purification, crystallization and drying, to produce potassium sulfate. The extreme evaporation that makes Lop Nur so inhospitable does much of the concentrating naturally. Water scarcity has also shaped the production system. Fresh water has to be piped in from Ruoqiang, about 240 kilometers away, while liquids left from processing are recycled within the system and brine is not discharged outside it. Inside the plant, progress has often been measured in fractions of a percentage point. Dong Guangfeng, head of the potassium sulfate plant, arrived in 2005, when there was only an industrial pilot facility. Over the following two decades, he and his colleagues worked to raise potassium content and develop a wider range of products. The potassium oxide content of the company's potassium sulfate has risen from 51 percent to a stable 52.5 percent, while a high-end product reaches 53.8 percent. Its product range has also expanded to include granular and water-soluble fertilizers. China's potash self-sufficiency has now risen to around 50 percent, Dong said, with Lop Nur contributing an important share of domestic supply. The brine is also yielding another product. In 2023, the company put into operation a line that extracts lithium from residual brine after potash production. The facility can produce 5,000 tonnes of lithium carbonate a year, mainly for use in power batteries for new energy vehicles. A TOWN TAKES ROOT The industry has also drawn people. Chen Liangzhi, from southwest China's Sichuan Province, was among the early arrivals. When he came to Lop Nur in 2000, there were no roads, electricity or running water. He lived in a semi-underground shelter and ran a restaurant from a prefabricated metal room. At midday in summer, when surface temperatures could reach 50 to 60 degrees Celsius, the room became too hot for cooking. Chen would retreat underground and wait until late afternoon before lighting the stove again. Today, his restaurant covers more than 100 square meters and serves business travelers. Lop Nur Town was formally established in 2002. Its water, electricity and heating are largely supplied via facilities operated by the potash company, while garbage and sewage are handled through shared facilities. Medical workers from the People's Hospital of Bayingolin Mongolian Autonomous Prefecture are stationed at the local clinic. "If you want people to stay, you first have to make them feel secure about living here," said Liu Xiangyu, deputy Party secretary of Lop Nur Town. Over 3,000 people now live in the settlement that grew around the potash industry. Notably, far beyond Lop Nur, potassium from beneath its salt crust is reaching and nourishing farmlands across China.

item.title: Philippine warship 'trailing' Chinese aircraft carrier Liaoning? The whole world is laughing: Global Times editorial
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-28 00:31:00
The Liaoning aircraft carrier participates in a dual-aircraft-carrier formation drill on October 21, 2024. Photo: VCG The Philippine side is well aware of the consequences of recklessly provoking China, yet it has still pressed ahead with this self-staged farce. The root cause is that certain forces in the Philippines want to stir up trouble in the South China Sea to contain China, but lack the confidence and capabilities to back up any substantive confrontational moves. All they can do is resort to this shoddy performance to bluff and create a false impression of strength. Recently, during a new round of multilateral maritime cooperative activity involving the US, Japan and the Philippines, Manila dispatched a vessel to follow the Liaoning aircraft carrier group. At most, the Philippine vessel trailed the Chinese carrier group from a distance and snapped a few photos. Yet the Philippine side hyped this up as an operation to "track" and "monitor" the Chinese navy. Judging solely by the rhetoric of some Philippine military figures and media outlets, one might assume that Manila had deployed a formidable naval force. But once all the relevant facts are considered, the true nature of this guilty-minded performance becomes clear. The aircraft carrier Liaoning 's training activities in the relevant waters of the Western Pacific are routine arrangements under its annual training plan, consistent with international law and international practice, and not directed against any particular country or target. As the group navigated through the high seas and archipelagic sea lanes, it exercised the rights of navigation and passage guaranteed under international law. Throughout the voyage, the group maintained a professional and restrained posture and did not take any hostile action against the Philippines. Even a Philippine Coast Guard spokesperson had to acknowledge that "the movement could still fall within internationally recognized navigational rights." The BRP Sarangani, the Philippine vessel involved in the operation, was originally a decommissioned patrol and rescue vessel donated by the Taiwan authorities. Given its size, its so-called "tracking" of a large combat formation such as an aircraft carrier group could amount to little more than symbolic shadowing from a distance. It could neither approach the aircraft carrier group nor gather much valuable intelligence, let alone establish any meaningful monitoring capability. The Philippine side is well aware of the consequences of recklessly provoking China, yet it has still pressed ahead with this self-staged farce. The root cause is that certain forces in the Philippines want to stir up trouble in the South China Sea to contain China, but lack the confidence and capabilities to back up any substantive confrontational moves. All they can do is resort to this shoddy performance to bluff and create a false impression of strength. Looking deeper, this maneuver is driven both by domestic political calculations in the Philippines and by a desire to appease external powers. Faced with challenges such as sluggish economic growth and mounting pressure on the government, Manila is attempting to divert public attention by hyping up external "threats" and projecting an image of being "tough on the outside," thereby reaping political capital for the administration. Meanwhile, the Philippines has been stepping up military cooperation with the US, Japan and other countries. Publicizing details of its so-called "monitoring" of the Liaoning aircraft carrier group amid joint US-Japan-Philippines exercises serves to demonstrate its value to external allies in maintaining a "forward presence" and to show that it can make tangible contributions, even if that "contribution" amounts to nothing more than a decommissioned small vessel trailing the carrier group from a distance. It is also an attempt to enlist external support to bolster its position in maritime disputes and exploit regional tensions for unwarranted gains. But no matter how inflated the bubble of rhetoric becomes, it cannot deliver real security. Some in the Philippines also need to carefully consider the costs of their blind faith in courting powers from outside the region. Certain external powers are willing to put the Philippines on the front line because doing so serves their own strategic interests. This does not mean, however, that they are prepared to bear the consequences of every risky move Manila makes. Should an incident occur at sea, Philippine vessels and personnel would be closest to the scene, and the Philippines itself would be the first to bear the risks. Pinning the country's maritime security on the appearance of backing from others not only overestimates the practical value of that retired patrol boat but also underestimates the price the Philippines itself would have to pay if regional tensions escalated. In fact, what truly threatens regional security is the Philippines' provocations in the South China Sea and its collusion with the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities in Taiwan island. The Taiwan question is particularly sensitive. Any move that could blur the boundaries of the one-China policy or extend security cooperation into sensitive areas risks triggering major upheaval in the region. On the one hand, Manila reiterates its adherence to the one-China policy; on the other, it allows coast guard equipment from the Taiwan region to enter the ranks of its coast guard. Such double-dealing is playing with fire. China remains unwavering in its commitment to safeguarding national sovereignty and maritime rights and interests, while consistently advocating negotiations to manage differences. The Liaoning aircraft carrier's voyages into distant waters are a normal milestone in China's defense modernization. Its course will not be altered by the trailing of one or two decommissioned patrol vessels, nor will it be diverted by the clamor surrounding a handful of joint military exercises. Manila must understand that stirring up trouble with the backing of external powers will not bring it genuine security. It will only draw the Philippines deeper into a complex geopolitical game.

item.title: GT Voice: China's AI stock pullback isn't a signal of a 'bubble bursting'
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27 22:14:00
AI Photo: VCG The recent lackluster performance of China's STAR 50 Index, which tracks the 50 largest stocks on the sci-tech innovation board, has drawn attention, with some Western media outlets seizing on the pullback to draw misleading conclusions about the country's artificial intelligence (AI) development. Reuters on Monday published an article headlined "In China, the AI bubble has already burst," interpreting the drop in the AI-heavy STAR 50 Index and the contraction in the market capitalization of AI-related listed companies as the bursting of bubbles. Short-term stock price fluctuations reflect shifts in capital preferences, market expectations and valuations, and they do not necessarily signal a reversal in an industry's fundamentals. To equate an index decline with a "bursting bubble," and to treat capital market movements as a denial of China's AI industry prospects, is logically untenable and gives a misleading picture of China's technological development. Capital markets naturally experience cycles of rising and falling expectations and valuation corrections, and volatility in sci-tech innovation sectors is particularly fierce. This is a common phenomenon in global financial markets. The sharp pullback in AI and semiconductor-related stocks this round is essentially a correction of the overheated valuations of some targets in the earlier period, and a rational cooling of capital from excessive expectations, rather than a shake-up of the industrial foundation. Figures are more than enough to break the one-sided narrative of the "bubble theory." According to Minister of Industry and Information Technology Li Lecheng, China's core AI industry was valued at more than 1.2 trillion yuan ($173.9 billion) in 2025, as the technology is emerging as a powerful driver for high-quality economic development. AI is increasingly being deployed across factories and daily life in China. As of the end of 2025, more than 30 percent of manufacturing enterprises with annual main business turnover of at least 20 million yuan had adopted AI technologies, while Chinese companies had released more than 300 humanoid robot products. Data released at a State Council Information Office press conference shows that as of the end of June 2026, China's intelligent computing capacity reached 2,185 EFLOPS (Exa Floating-point Operations Per Second), a year-on-year surge of 177 percent, and the overall utilization rate of computing facilities nationwide stood at 71.4 percent. Even more symbolic is that Chinese AI large-language models recorded usage of 93.54 trillion tokens for the week ending October 25, marking 26 consecutive weeks of global leadership, according to data from OpenRouter. This figure shows that the vitality of China's domestic AI application ecosystem has entered the global first tier. These indicators certainly cannot replace profitability, nor can they guarantee that every enterprise will succeed, but they at least show that China's AI sector has a continuously expanding base, a growing number of market players and large-scale computing power support. Given such extensive industrial activity, it is obviously biased to claim that the entire industry is a "bubble that has burst" based solely on a phase of stock price adjustment. Judging the real prospects of a high-tech industry comes down to technological capability, commercial application and economic returns. Whether technology continues to advance and can operate reliably in complex scenarios, and whether applications are moving toward large-scale adoption and can help improve efficiency in manufacturing, healthcare, transportation, education and other sectors - these are the far more meaningful criteria. This process cannot be achieved overnight, nor will it change direction because of a few stock price swings. When evaluating China's science and technology industries, Western media outlets tend to swing between two extremes. When growth is rapid, it portrays China as an "unstoppable threat" and when the market adjusts, it rushes to declare "the bursting of bubbles." These two seemingly opposite narratives actually share the same problem: they are unwilling to understand China's development with a long-term and professional vision. China's AI sector should neither be overestimated nor underestimated. What it needs is continuous innovation, effective competition, and patient capital, rather than being led by short-term noise. In the end, the long-term value of China's AI development will stand the test of time through sustained technological progress, widespread commercial adoption and solid real economic returns. Separating short-term market sentiment from long-term industrial trends is far closer to the facts and carries far more analytical value than simply slapping on a "burst bubble" label.

item.title: Mbappé's lesson: Talent opens doors, respect keeps them open
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27 16:30:00
Kylian Mbappé Photo: VCG A football star can make hundreds of millions on the pitch, only to lose the trust of an entire market by failing to show the most basic respect. French football star Kylian Mbappé has recently sparked a fierce backlash in China after making extremely inappropriate remarks in a recent interview. What did he say? Many Chinese would rather not repeat it. Dongqiudi, a major Chinese football news and community platform, issued a statement saying that it would not translate the interview because the footballer's remarks had hurt the feelings of Chinese fans and the Chinese people. Brands including Dongpeng Beverage Group and Chinese dairy giant Mengniu promptly terminated their cooperation. This is not an emotional outburst, but a rational choice made spontaneously by the market. On Tuesday, Mbappé apologized. In a statement, he wrote "my comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world." The lesson is clear: Respect is not optional; one doesn't get to profit from China while disrespecting it. Not a chance. Mbappé's talent and skills are beyond doubt. But talent and public responsibility are two entirely different things. The first determines how many goals you score and how much you are worth; the second determines how many people are still willing to pay for you. Talent may open the door to a market, but respect is what keeps it open. We don't know whether Mbappé would deliberately set out to offend a country whose market has helped fuel his commercial success. One thing is for sure: He lacks cross-cultural awareness, and fails to appreciate the responsibilities that come with global fame. Had he shown even a basic understanding of Chinese culture and sensitivities, he might have thought twice before speaking so disrespectfully. Every culture has its boundaries. That is no secret. No one expects a foreign athlete to be an expert on China. But global superstars who have long profited from commercial partnerships in China should make an effort to understand the country's cultural sensitivities and show a basic level of respect. That is not asking for special treatment. It is basic commercial common sense. For Chinese brands, terminating such cooperation is no small decision. Previous marketing investments, contractual obligations and the cost of replacing promotional materials all mean real costs. Yet, by cutting ties, these companies are sending a clear message: When public sentiment is offended, businesses cannot pretend nothing has happened. China's market remains open and welcomes athletes and brands from around the world to share in its opportunities. But an open market is not a market without boundaries. The threshold is respect. Those who disregard the feelings of the Chinese people should not expect to escape the commercial consequences. For decades, some international public figures have been happy to take the money from the Chinese market while talking carelessly about China. When it comes to matters of principle, they tend to dismiss offensive remarks as "personal expression" or hide behind "freedom of speech." That's no excuse. This time, Mbappé has learned the hard way. His case should serve as a clear red line for every foreign public figure hoping to profit from China: On issues of national sentiment, no one has the freedom to act recklessly. Going forward, our commercial contracts might as well spell out clearer clauses governing public conduct. The national feelings of the Chinese people are not to be provoked, and the Chinese market will leave no room for those who display arrogance and disrespect.
